description: GPOCompare mapping catalog for translating normalized GPO settings to Microsoft Intune migration targets.

statusDefinitions.DirectCategory: A direct Intune policy category exists. Validate semantics before migrating.
statusDefinitions.Review: A target area exists but each setting must be reviewed and mapped individually.
statusDefinitions.Discover: Search Intune (Settings Catalog / ADMX-backed) for the exact setting name.
statusDefinitions.NoDirectReplacement: No generic Intune equivalent. Assess per setting.
statusDefinitions.Unmapped: Set by the script when no mapping entry matches the setting.
statusDefinitions.MappingFileMissing: Set by the script when this file was not found.

mappings.notes: Match the individual user-right name to the corresponding Intune Account protection setting where exposed. Preserve assigned principals.
Security Options coverage varies. Resolve the exact normalized setting name before migration.
Evaluate Settings Catalog coverage for the specific service; otherwise use an approved management method such as remediation where appropriate.
Fallback for Security settings without a more specific entry, such as account policies (password, lockout, Kerberos). Identify the equivalent Settings Catalog setting before migration.
Search Intune by the exact ADMX policy name. Do not assume equivalence solely from the display name.
Search Intune by the exact ADMX policy name and confirm user scope.
Map the exact audit subcategory and preserve Success/Failure selection.
Firewall profile settings belong under Microsoft Defender Firewall policies. Validate per-profile semantics.
A registry value alone does not prove the supported Intune path. Identify the backing CSP/ADMX before using Custom or remediation.
Convert GPP group membership intent to Local user group membership and verify add/replace semantics.
Each member is its own setting: SettingName is '<group> member: <member>' and the value is the GPP action. Translate add/remove actions carefully; GPP action semantics are not always one-to-one.
NRPT and encrypted name-resolution settings require rule-by-rule validation. Do not generate an OMA-URI without a confirmed Policy CSP mapping.

firewallRuleMapping.intuneType: Endpoint security > Firewall > Microsoft Defender Firewall Rules
firewallRuleMapping.notes: Inbound and Outbound rules are parsed. Address scopes are not parsed by the module, so they cannot yet be mapped from this catalog.
